newsitem.title: USA: NYMEX heat ends off, distillate stock surplus seen.
newsitem.headline: NYMEX heat ends off, distillate stock surplus seen.

text.p: NYMEX heating oil prices declined Tuesday on expectations oil inventory data would show a year-over-year surplus in distillate stocks for the first time in more than a year.

"If we don't have a decline of five million barrels or more like we did last year at this time, these stats could show a surplus, which was bound to pressure March heating oil," said ING Derivatives analyst Tom Bentz.
March heating oil settled off 1.10 cents a gallon at 64.18 cents.
Caught under heat's downdraft, March crude ended off 13 cents a barrel at $24.02 while March gasoline ended off 0.04 cent a gallon at 68.31 cents.

Dealers expect the American Petroleum Institute (API) to show a decline in distillate stocks (comprised of heating oil and diesel) of between two and three million barrels for the week ended January 31.

Distillate stocks usually decline during this time of year, and a particularly large amount of seasonal refinery maintenance is also cutting output. But, a more severe winter caused a five million barrel decline this time last year.
This year's milder weather has slackened heating oil demand, tempering distillate stock declines and creating fuller inventories versus year ago, dealers said.
The last distillate surplus was a meager 522,000 barrels in June 1995.
Two extended winters in 1995 and 1996 left distillate stocks bare, with the year-over-year shortfall reaching 20 million barrels last August.
High distillate output has replenished distillate stocks to near year ago levels.

Also pressuring heat Tuesday was talk of a major player having taken delivery of a large amount of heating oil amid the deteriorated buying interest. The player may need to sell the supply cheaper than it wanted to, dealers said.
Talk of the heating oil deliveries on the expired February contract centered on midcontinent producer/refiner Koch Oil. Koch was not immediately available to comment.
The NYMEX said PaineWebber Inc accepted a total 2,159 lots, with traders in futures and cash markets pointing to Koch as the main player for whom PaineWebber had cleared those barrels.
Meanwhile, chartists said prompt heating oil looked technically weak after the spot month hit a session low of 63.55 cents, breaking 64.30, tested support and March's low since mid-December.
-- Harry Milling, New York Energy Desk, 212-859-1761
